Extended H-Index Centrality

Source: R/centrality-batch68.R
centrality_ehc.Rd

The extended H-index centrality (EHC; Zareie and Sheikhahmadi 2019) adds over a node's neighbors a weighted count of the degrees of their own neighbors: $$EHC(i) = \sum_{j \in N(i)} CMC(j), \qquad CMC(j) = \sum_{k=1}^{h} p^{1 + kp/r} c_k(j),$$ with \(c_k(j)\) the number of neighbors of \(j\) of degree at least \(k\) and \(h\) the largest degree of the network.

Usage

centrality_ehc(x, ...)

Arguments

x

Network input accepted by centrality.

...

Further arguments to centrality. The measure uses ehc_p (default 0.8) and ehc_r (default 100).

Value

A named numeric vector with one score per node, in input node order.

Details

The measure is computed on the simple undirected skeleton of the network, so direction, weights, loops and parallel edges are ignored. ehc_p = 0.8 and ehc_r = 100 are the authors' values (their Section 4.3). The source gives \([0, 1]\) as the range of both parameters but uses \(r\) from 1 to 10000; ehc_p must lie in \((0, 1]\) and ehc_r be above 0. Since \(\sum_k c_k(j)\) is the sum of the degrees of the neighbors of \(j\), CMC is that sum with the units of degree weighted by the slowly decreasing \(p^{1 + kp/r}\); at ehc_p = 1 EHC is the sum, over the walks of two steps from the node, of the degree of the node reached. Despite its name the measure ranks nodes far from the h-index family. An isolated node scores 0. With ehc_p = 0.5 and ehc_r = 10 the implementation reproduces the worked example on the source's Fig. 1: the largest degree 7, the two printed cumulative vectors, the 12 printed CMC values and \(EHC(1) = 21.616\), \(EHC(3) = 42.106\). The source prints a monotonicity of 0.9612 on the karate club, above 0.9542, the largest value an exact structural measure can reach there, which is the value of the implementation; its monotonicity on the dolphins network (0.9979) is reproduced and is also the largest possible there. On four test networks the score ranks nodes closest to centrality_ninl (mean Kendall correlation 0.985, 0.997 on one network) and centrality_diffusion_centrality (0.983); with centrality_semilocal the correlation is 0.91 to 0.92. A ehc_p outside \((0, 1]\) or a ehc_r that is not a finite number above 0 raises a cograph_bad_parameter error. Over the 19 networks of the package's correlation audit the mean correlation with diffusion_centrality is 0.995 (0.981 at the least). normalized = TRUE divides the scores by their maximum.

References

Zareie, A. and Sheikhahmadi, A. (2019). EHC: extended H-index centrality measure for identification of users' spreading influence in complex networks. Physica A: Statistical Mechanics and its Applications, 514, 141-155. doi:10.1016/j.physa.2018.09.064 .

See also

centrality_lobby, centrality_diffusion_centrality, centrality_ninl, centrality.

Examples

centrality_ehc(regulation_net)
#>    Explore       Plan    Monitor      Adapt    Reflect    Discuss Synthesize 
#>   117.7042   144.7222   163.8169   139.9535   116.1042   118.5156   100.2265 
#>   Evaluate     Create      Share 
#>   126.4714   146.3264   127.2657 
centrality_ehc(regulation_net, ehc_p = 0.5, ehc_r = 10)
#>    Explore       Plan    Monitor      Adapt    Reflect    Discuss Synthesize 
#>   66.10316   81.05179   91.85468   78.40366   65.10770   66.72017   56.47797 
#>   Evaluate     Create      Share 
#>   71.21751   82.08875   71.65179
